text:
alex: Heads-up — during the Karpenter migration smoke tests in us-west-2 we hit a cluster-level flapping issue where GPU nodes were Pending for >10m with IP allocation errors. paste of the node events below.

alex: Events: 
```
  Normal  Scheduled  5m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned gpu/worker-xyz to i-0abcde
  Warning FailedAttachVolume  5m  attachdetach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "eni-attach": failed to allocate IP: ENI quota exhausted
  Warning  FailedScheduling  4m  kube-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient memory, 4 Insufficient allocatable pods
```

maria: What’s the provisioner config? any nodeSelector/zone constraints?

alex: prototype Karpenter provisioner: `provisioner.gpu-prod` w/ zones [us-west-2a,2b], `requirements: kubernetes.io/arch = amd64`, `instanceTypes: p4.*, g5.*`, `ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 30`, `consolidation: enabled`. No warm pool configured yet.

jamie: Sounds like IP exhaustion + burst of pod requests. Could be ENI limits per instance type + pod density. Also if consolidation is enabled, terminated nodes may not free IPs fast enough for new nodes. :thinking:

maria: Do we have ENI trunking enabled on those instance families? trunking reduces pod-to-ENI contention.

alex: Not on the test account. We treated this as a migration proof-of-concept; default VPC settings.

sre-oncall: Recommend immediate mitigations: 1) reduce consolidation window (or disable) to avoid chasing capacity, 2) set `maxPods` via kubelet config or `overhead` in provisioner to limit density, 3) add a small warm pool (2-3 nodes) for p4/g5 to smooth spikes.

jamie: Also confirm subnet IP usage across AZs — we hit imbalanced subnet allocation previously. Karpenter may be picking healthy AZs that are low on prefix capacity.

alex: Agreed. I saw most pending nodes in 2b where subnet free IPs were 6. Two new node requests asked for >10 pods each.

maria: For longer-term: Enable ENI trunking on instance types and add fallback instance types with higher ENI capacity (e.g., move some workloads to m6i/g5a mix while we calibrate).

alex: Quick test plan I propose:
- step 1: disable consolidation on the provisioner and run another load test.
- step 2: create a tiny warm pool (2 p4 nodes) via manual scaling in the test cluster.
- step 3: update provisioner to include `overhead` so pods won’t pack >50 pods per instance.
- step 4: re-run smoke and capture kubelet/kube-proxy logs.

jamie: also add a conservative `startupProbe` and `podDisruptionBudget` for the training pods so Karpenter doesn’t immediately evict them during churn.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1423 for the warm-pool + provisioner tuning work (link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFRA-1423) :white_check_mark:

maria: Cost note: warm pools increase committed spend. If we keep 2 p4 nodes idle that's ~2 x reserved hourly. We should measure tail latency improvement vs cost. If we can safely use smaller instances for warm pool and burst to p4 only on demand, do that.

alex: Good point — we can try warm pool with cheaper instances (g5a.xlarge) that have ENI headroom, then let Karpenter pick p4 when needed.

sre-oncall: Long term items: add capacity-aware routing in Karpenter settings (prefer instance types with more ENI), add a probe to detect subnet exhaustion and mark AZ as soft-avoid, and update docs on ENI quotas per region.

jamie: For the migration checklist, add a step to validate `maxPods` and ENI/trunking for each instance type, and run across all AZs to catch subnet fragmentation.

alex: Will run the test steps this afternoon and post results here. If we see repro, we may pause migration until we have warm pool + `overhead` tuned.

maria: Thanks — ping me after the run, I’ll check cost analysis and help craft rollout guardrails. :thumbsup:

alex: update (1h later): after disabling consolidation + spinning 2 g5a warm nodes, pending time dropped from 12m -> 30s for the same load. Still seeing one pod OOM on a p4-scaled node — investigating config.

jamie: Nice. That suggests consolidation + cold starts were the main culprit. Keep an eye on ENI errors though.

infra-bot: INFRA-1423 status updated: in-progress -> testing.

sre-oncall: If you need a quick quota bump request for ENIs in us-west-2, I can escalate with cloud support.

alex: Thanks — will loop you in if we repro consistently.

maria: wrapping up — let's document the final prov config we land on and add a short runbook for ENI exhaustion during migration.

alex: agreed. Will add notes to the ticket and upload the provisioner YAML + test logs.
